review_notes: I read the whole file. It has 16 near-identical `singlePairNNN` theorems (136–151), and each ends with a `norm_num [...] at hp ⊢; linarith only [hp]` step. I checked `Sparse.eval` and its simp lemmas in Certificate/Algebra.lean. `Sparse.eval_nil` and `Sparse.eval_cons` are already `@[simp]` and proved by `rfl`. I also checked that `PairSemantics.valueN` and `singlePairValueN` are plain `def`s of explicit lists. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about loops or about the simplifier's behaviour in practice. I found no rewrite-direction problem or cycle. The only issue is how the simp interface is used.

findings.excerpt: norm_num [singlePairValue136, PairSemantics.value0, PairSemantics.value4, PairSemantics.value9, PairSemantics.value45, PairSemantics.value151, Sparse.eval] at hp ⊢
findings.problem: Each theorem passes the unfolding of `Sparse.eval` to `norm_num`, although `Sparse.eval_nil` and `Sparse.eval_cons` are already `@[simp]` and are the intended canonical rewrite rules for explicit lists. The extra `Sparse.eval` unfolding is a second, competing route. It rewrites `eval` to `List.map` and `List.sum` and bypasses the dedicated lemmas. It also unfolds `eval` on `familyPairVector B` and on the matrix-moment terms, so more of the goal gets expanded than the argument needs. Each call also lists by hand the `singlePairValueN` def and every `PairSemantics.valueK` it uses, and these lists are copied by hand into all 16 theorems. A wrong or missing name in any list is easy to introduce, and the lists carry no information beyond what `hm0`–`hm4` already state. The values are plain `def`s of explicit lists with no equation lemma or simp set of their own, so every use has to name them.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `Sparse.eval` from the `norm_num` list and rely on the existing `@[simp]` lemmas `Sparse.eval_nil` and `Sparse.eval_cons`. Keep only the value defs that need unfolding. Better, state the value expansions once as `@[simp]` lemmas, or in a dedicated simp set that `norm_num` can call as `norm_num [pairValues]`. For example, `Sparse.eval PairSemantics.value46 x = (-1/60 : ℚ) * x 0 + ...` would let each theorem call `norm_num [singlePairValueN_eval]` or `simp` with a single shared set, instead of a per-theorem list of 5–7 def names.
findings.benefit: The normal form becomes one explicit linear combination of `familyPairVector B i` terms, built by the canonical `eval_cons` and `eval_nil` rules. Hand-maintained name lists disappear from 16 theorems, and the generator of this file no longer has to track which `valueK` each node uses.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem eval_cons (p : ι × ℚ) (v : Sparse ι) (x : ι → ℝ) :
    eval (p :: v) x = (p.2 : ℝ) * x p.1 + eval v x := rfl

noncomputable def eval (v : Sparse ι) (x : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (v.map fun p => (p.2 : ℝ) * x p.1).sum
